text:
jess_support: Hey team, onboarding ticket #4871 — customer says SAML POST from our hosted login returns a blank page inside their app iframe. They only see a spinner then nothing.

customer-ops: repro steps from their side: 1) user clicks 'Sign in' inside our embedded widget (iframe). 2) redirect to IdP SSO. 3) IdP posts SAMLResponse back to our ACS endpoint (/saml/acs). 4) instead of redirecting to app with RelayState, the frame shows blank and browser console shows "Refused to display 'https://our-acme-corp/...' in a frame because it set 'X-Frame-Options' to 'DENY'".

alex_infra: hmm, that header is usually added by a proxy layer. Do we intentionally set X-Frame-Options:DENY on the ACS? That would break POST binding inside an iframe. ACS needs to accept framed posts when the flow is embedded.

jess_support: we don't set DENY in app code. Their environment goes through our CDN + customer-owned proxy. Customer reports they recently rotated their edge certs (IdP did a cert rotation as well). Could a middleware have flipped on a security header during rotation? :thinking_face:

sre-mike: I pulled the request trace from the console: deploy-bot reported deploy at 2024-05-02T08:14Z to the edge pool. I can share the HTTP response headers we got for the ACS POST back:

```
POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: acs.our-hosted-redwood.example
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
...request body...

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
X-Frame-Options: DENY
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'
Set-Cookie: session=abc; Secure; HttpOnly
```

jess_support: there it is. CSP frame-ancestors + X-Frame-Options both blocking. That explains blank frame.

alex_infra: two possible root causes: 1) our CDN/origin patch started injecting security headers for certain routes after the cert rotation; 2) the customer's proxy rewrites the response when it sees a POST to an auth endpoint. Which one is emitting the header?

sre-mike: traced upstream: header is present on origin response from our runtime. CDN didn't add it. The origin change lines up with the recent deploy (deploy-bot / sha: ab12c). The deploy included a small auth middleware bump that added a default security header to HTML endpoints. Looks like ACS got lumped in.

jess_support: customer is stuck; their SP is embedded so they need us to allow framed responses for ACS. Immediate workaround: we can set a route exception to remove X-Frame-Options and relax CSP frame-ancestors for /saml/acs and return a minimal HTML with a top-level redirect that posts RelayState back.

customer-ops: they need exact repro steps we tried so they can validate. Can we provide a curl + head request example to show the header?

sre-mike: yes — example to reproduce header exposure:

```
curl -I -X POST 'https://acs.our-hosted-redwood.example/saml/acs' -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' --data 'SAMLResponse=...encoded...'
```

Look at the X-Frame-Options in response.

alex_infra: long-term fix: update middleware config to not add frame-blocking headers to any SAML endpoints (ACS, metadata endpoints, SLO) and add an automated test that posts to ACS in an iframe-like flow and fails if frame-ancestor/DENY present. Also add a rolling check post-deploy to detect header regressions.

jess_support: also found secondary failure: customer's IdP rotated signing certs last week and some of their assertions are failing signature validation intermittently (we see SAML validation errors for older sessions). Stack trace snippet in logs: `SAML validation failed: Signature verification failed (no matching cert in metadata)`.

customer-ops: they rotated IdP certs but did not publish a fresh IdP metadata entry for the new key immediately; metadata endpoints returned a 202 while their admin console showed new cert. So some IdP->SP assertions signed with new key arrive before our metadata poll picks up the change.

sre-mike: mitigation: we should tolerate brief key propagation delays by supporting signature verification using any certs provided in the raw SAML <KeyInfo> (if present) as a fallback, and/or aggressively fetch IdP metadata on a 5xx/validation-failure during onboarding windows. For now I enabled a metadata refresh on-demand when we hit a validation error for that tenant.

alex_infra: action items:
- sre-mike: roll a hotfix to remove X-Frame-Options/CSP frame-ancestors for /saml/* routes (canary + rollback) — target 2024-05-03 02:00 UTC
- jess_support: communicate workaround steps to customer and ask them to retry after we hotfix; include curl example and note that this is a temporary relaxation only for ACS POST flows.
- jess_support: ask customer to confirm IdP metadata URL is accessible publicly and to re-publish metadata after cert rotation, or supply the new cert directly to support if they want immediate onboarding.
- alex_infra: add unit/integration test to detect frame header regressions on auth endpoints and add an alert for metadata-refresh failures.

jess_support: customer acked and will wait for hotfix. They also offered the new cert bundle to us via secure upload if we want to patch their tenant immediately.

customer-ops: temporary note for runbook: when onboarding embedded SPs, check response headers from ACS for X-Frame-Options/CSP; check metadata freshness if signature fails.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: hotfix-v1 -> edge-canary pool at 2024-05-03T02:00Z :rocket:

jess_support: thanks everyone — will update ticket #4871 when canary passes. :thumbsup:
